# Detailed solution - R526

**Approach.** With its noise voltage in series with the gate, $M_6$ is a common-source stage degenerated by the resistance at node D (just $r_{O8}$) and loaded by the resistance looking down into $M_4$. KCL at D and Y gives the exact degenerated-CS gain. The gain from $M_8$'s gate to Y follows from a Norton equivalent, and the two are compared in voltage gain and in output noise power.

### Step 1 — The half circuit and the resistances around $M_6$

In the right half circuit (nodes B, Y, D), P and all bias lines are AC grounds.

- **Node D:** $M_8$ has its gate at $V_{b3}$ and its source at $V_{DD}$, so it presents just $r_{O8}$ from D to AC ground.
- **Body effect of $M_6$:** its bulk is tied to its source, so $v_{bs6} = 0$ and $g_{mb6}$ plays no role.
- **Below Y:** looking down into the drain of $M_4$ (gate at $V_{b1}$, bulk at ground), whose source B is degenerated by $r_{O2}$:
$$R_D = \left[1 + (g_{m4} + g_{mb4})\,r_{O4}\right]r_{O2} + r_{O4} .$$

### Step 2 — Small-signal model for the noise of $M_6$

With $V_{n6}$ in series with the gate, $v_{g6} = V_{n6}$. Node D has $r_{O8}$ to ground, node Y has $R_D$ to ground, and between them sit $M_6$'s controlled source $g_{m6}v_{gs6}$ (from drain Y to source D) and $r_{O6}$, with $v_{gs6} = V_{n6} - v_D$.

<!-- diagram: diagram-01.cir -->

The current $i$ inside $M_6$ from Y to D is

$$i = g_{m6}(V_{n6} - v_D) + \frac{v_Y - v_D}{r_{O6}} .$$

It leaves at D through $r_{O8}$ and is drawn at Y from ground through $R_D$:

$$v_D = i\,r_{O8},\qquad v_Y = -i\,R_D .$$

### Step 3 — Solve for the gain of $M_6$'s noise to Y

Substituting $v_D$ and $v_Y$ into the device equation:

$$i = g_{m6}V_{n6} - g_{m6}r_{O8}\,i - \frac{(R_D + r_{O8})\,i}{r_{O6}} ,$$

$$i\left(r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8} + R_D + r_{O8}\right) = g_{m6}r_{O6}V_{n6},$$

$$i = \frac{g_{m6}r_{O6}V_{n6}}{R_D + r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}} .$$

Then $v_Y = -iR_D$ gives

$$\boxed{A_6 = \frac{v_Y}{V_{n6}} = -\frac{g_{m6}r_{O6}R_D}{R_D + r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}}}$$

the exact gain of a degenerated common-source stage with $R_S = r_{O8}$, $g_{mb} = 0$ and load $R_D$.

With the resistance looking up into the drain of $M_6$,

$$R_{up} = (1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})\,r_{O8} + r_{O6} = r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8},$$

and the total resistance at Y, $R_{out} = R_{up}\parallel R_D = R_DR_{up}/(R_D + R_{up})$, the gain becomes

$$|A_6| = \frac{g_{m6}r_{O6}}{R_{up}}\,R_{out} \approx \frac{R_{out}}{r_{O8}}\qquad(g_{m6}r_{O6} \gg 1,\ \text{so } R_{up} \approx g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}).$$

The degenerated $M_6$ has an effective transconductance of only $\approx 1/r_{O8}$: its gate voltage can drive current only through $r_{O8}$, because $M_8$ is a current source.

### Step 4 — Gain seen by the noise of $M_8$

Now put $V_{n8}$ in series with the gate of $M_8$ and set $V_{n6} = 0$. $M_8$ (source at $V_{DD}$) is a controlled source $g_{m8}V_{n8}$ drawn from D to ground (drain-to-source convention; the sign does not affect the noise power), and $M_6$ acts as a common-gate cascode between D and Y.

<!-- diagram: diagram-02.cir -->

**Norton approach.** With Y grounded, $M_6$ presents the source resistance $r_{O6}/(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})$ at D, so the current $g_{m8}V_{n8}$ divides between $r_{O8}$ and $M_6$, and the short-circuit current through $M_6$ is

$$i_{sc} = g_{m8}V_{n8}\,\frac{r_{O8}}{r_{O8} + \dfrac{r_{O6}}{1 + g_{m6}r_{O6}}} = g_{m8}V_{n8}\,\frac{r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})}{r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6}) + r_{O6}} = g_{m8}V_{n8}\,\frac{r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})}{R_{up}} \approx g_{m8}V_{n8}.$$

Almost all of $M_8$'s current passes through the cascode, whose source is a low-impedance point compared with $r_{O8}$. The output resistance at Y is the same $R_{out}$, so

$$|A_8| = \frac{g_{m8}r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})}{R_{up}}\,R_{out} = \frac{g_{m8}r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})\,R_D}{R_D + r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}} \approx g_{m8}R_{out}.$$

(Solving the two node equations directly gives the same expression.)

### Step 5 — Compare $M_6$ with $M_8$

**Voltage gains.** The common denominator and $R_D$ cancel:

$$\frac{|A_6|}{|A_8|} = \frac{g_{m6}r_{O6}}{g_{m8}r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m8}r_{O8}} .$$

**Noise powers.** With $\overline{V_n^2} = 4kT\gamma/g_m$ in series with each gate, the ratio of the output noise spectral densities at Y is

$$\frac{S_6}{S_8} = \frac{\overline{V_{n6}^2}\,A_6^2}{\overline{V_{n8}^2}\,A_8^2} = \frac{g_{m8}}{g_{m6}}\left(\frac{A_6}{A_8}\right)^2 \approx \frac{g_{m8}}{g_{m6}}\cdot\frac{1}{(g_{m8}r_{O8})^2} = \frac{1}{g_{m6}\,g_{m8}\,r_{O8}^2}.$$

$M_6$ and $M_8$ have the same size (320 µm/80 nm) and current (≈ 0.95 mA each), so $g_{m6} \approx g_{m8}$ and

$$\frac{S_6}{S_8} \approx \frac{1}{(g_{m8}r_{O8})^2}.$$

With long-channel devices ($g_mr_O \sim 50$–$100$) this is below 0.05 %, the usual textbook conclusion. Here the PMOS devices carry about 0.95 mA at only about 100 mV of $|V_{DS}|$ (the 1-V supply is shared by the whole stack), so $r_O$ is only a few hundred ohms and $g_{m8}r_{O8}$ only about 5–10:

$$\frac{S_6}{S_8} \approx \frac{1}{5^2}\ \text{to}\ \frac{1}{10^2} = 4\,\%\ \text{to}\ 1\,\%,$$

small but no longer negligible.

### Result

$M_6$'s gate noise sees a degenerated common-source stage with $R_S = r_{O8}$, no body effect, and load $R_D = [1 + (g_{m4} + g_{mb4})r_{O4}]r_{O2} + r_{O4}$:

$$A_6 = \frac{g_{m6}r_{O6}R_D}{R_D + r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}} \approx \frac{R_{out}}{r_{O8}},$$

with $R_{out} = R_{up}\parallel R_D$ and $R_{up} = r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}$. $M_8$'s gate noise sees

$$A_8 = \frac{g_{m8}r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})R_D}{R_D + r_{O8} + r_{O6} + g_{m6}r_{O6}r_{O8}} \approx g_{m8}R_{out}.$$

Hence $A_6/A_8 = g_{m6}r_{O6}/[g_{m8}r_{O8}(1 + g_{m6}r_{O6})] \approx 1/(g_{m8}r_{O8})$, and the output noise power of $M_6$ relative to $M_8$ is $\approx (g_{m8}/g_{m6})/(g_{m8}r_{O8})^2 \approx 1/(g_{m8}r_{O8})^2$. The cascode's noise is suppressed by the intrinsic gain of the current source. That is very effective for long-channel devices, but with $g_mr_O \approx 5$–10 in this 40-nm design $M_6$ still contributes roughly 1–4 % of $M_8$'s noise power.

**Common mistake.** Treating the source of $M_6$ as an AC ground, which gives a gain of $g_{m6}R_{out}$, as large as $M_8$'s. Node D is loaded only by $r_{O8}$, so $M_6$ is heavily degenerated.

**Common mistake.** Taking the degeneration as $1/g_{m8}$, as if $M_8$ were diode-connected. Its gate is held at $V_{b3}$, so its drain presents $r_{O8}$.

**Common mistake.** Including $g_{mb6}$ in the gain. The bulk of $M_6$ is tied to its source, so the term vanishes (the body effect of $M_4$, whose bulk is at ground, does appear inside $R_D$).
